title: Participation Is Not Collaboration: Tracing Public Ownership After Cross-Product Agent Review
description:
Reproducible analysis artifact for the EMSE 2026 Special Issue paper "Participation Is Not Collaboration: Tracing Public Ownership After Cross-Product Agent Review".

A pull request written by one coding-agent product and reviewed by another looks like a multi-agent workflow, but two products on one pull request do not show that either answered the other. We ask what connected public path follows one cross-product review comment. From one fixed version of the AIDev dataset we analyse 8,608 pull requests where one product reviewed another's change, 546 matched pairs, and a 1,067-request outcome group. Measured activity is anchored to that comment by exact account, comment, and review-batch identifiers. We set aside the first minutes of automated posting, count outcomes only after hour 48 so the exposure precedes the outcome, and re-test the rule with deliberately wrong anchors.

Direct dialogue between products is rare; once the opening minutes are set aside, people take most remaining first actions. Cross-product review draws 13 percentage points less visible follow-up than matched same-product review. A reply that GitHub records as answering the comment goes with 17 points more later merging, and a person writes it four times in five. The wrong-anchor tests then qualify that: a reply attached anywhere else does as well, and shuffling which comment each reply answers leaves the estimate unmoved. Reading all 105 replies, the association sits with those a person wrote, not with one-click hand-offs to another machine. Linking an issue in the request roughly doubles the chance a review point is answered across a product boundary, and changes nothing within one product. We conclude that public multi-agent impact should be reported as a map of connections, not a count of products, and that the trace shows retained human attention rather than a resolved review point.

The archive holds the analysis and figure code, the reproduction contract and protocol ledgers, the test suite, the licence files, the README, the citation metadata, a REPRODUCE.md written for someone who has the archive and nothing else, and the derived analysis products under outputs/ that the manuscript tables and figures are built from. MANIFEST.csv and SHA256SUMS cover every file in it.

The AIDev-7.6M release itself is not included. It is third-party data under its own terms and has its own home; the pinned revision is recorded here and in the code so a user can fetch exactly the same one. Also excluded, and asserted on at build time, are the private coder keys and answer keys that would de-blind the human-coding audits, the author-metadata audit, ad-hoc exploration scratch, and the submission-portal staging folder. The MIT licence covers the analysis code, figure code, build scripts, and the derived analysis products. It does not cover the AIDev-7.6M release or any other third-party dataset screened during the external-evidence audit, nor the manuscript text and figures, whose rights transfer is governed by the publisher agreement. See NOTICE.md in the archive.
